# PLAN — iteration 1

## Current state assessment

The incumbent has 7 LUTs, 9 FFs, routed setup WNS of 0.553 ns, and hold WHS of 0.135 ns, so timing is feasible and any promotion must strictly improve `(LUTs, FFs)`. The supplied seed passes the recorded simulation and implementation stages; its numeric top latency is unknown, so no numeric annotation is required. The PWM counter resets synchronously, wraps every 256 cycles, and `pwm_out` uses the pre-increment counter value.

## Hypothesis

Replacing the explicit terminal-count check with natural 8-bit overflow should preserve the 256-cycle count while removing wrap logic, potentially reducing LUT use without adding FFs or changing timing behavior.

## Instruction for generator

Change `counter` from 32 bits to 8 bits and replace the equality-and-reset/increment branch with an unconditional 8-bit increment on each non-reset clock; keep the synchronous reset and `pwm_out <= (counter < duty)` assignment unchanged. Preserve the existing ports and cycle behavior, including the registered output’s use of the old counter value and the duty value sampled on each clock. Do not add a numeric latency annotation because the authoritative top latency is unknown.
